record.title: China sets out national AI employment policy with worker-transition and job-risk measures
record.summary: China’s General Office of the State Council published an opinion on 23 October 2026 (document date 16 October) setting out 18 measures in six areas for an employment-focused response to AI development. It calls for AI-related job creation and training while also addressing adoption-related job risk, worker transitions, employment services, labor and social-security protections, income distribution, and monitoring. The text directs risk assessment for potentially high-impact AI applications in market-access areas and calls for cautious pacing in labor-intensive sectors. It establishes announced policy direction, not implementation, funding totals, or measured employment effects.
organizations: General Office of the State Council of the People’s Republic of China
Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The General Office of China’s State Council published Guobanfa [2026] No. 29 on 23 October 2026; the document metadata gives 16 October 2026 as its document date.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The opinion sets out 18 measures in six areas: promoting AI-related job creation and new occupations; managing employment effects of AI adoption, including risk assessment for potentially high-impact applications in market-access areas and transition support; skills training; AI-enabled employment services; labor and social-security protections; and monitoring and response to employment risks.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The opinion directs agencies to support AI entrepreneurship and SMEs, encourage human-machine collaboration, manage adoption pace in labor-intensive sectors, assess employment risks in relevant project reviews, and research distributional and labor effects. Its listed national AI investment fund is mentioned as an existing funding instrument; no new allocation amount is stated.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The publication establishes announced policy direction, not the legal force of each measure, local implementation, budget commitments, realized job creation/displacement, or measured labor-market outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: The opinion announces central policy direction but does not establish how individual measures will be implemented, their binding force, subordinate deadlines, responsible budgets or cross-province compliance.
No employment, wage, displacement, retraining or job-quality outcome is measured in the policy text.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented across Chinese ministries and provincial governments, an employment-focused AI policy spanning job creation, adoption risk assessment, worker transition support, skills and labor protections could materially shape AI diffusion and labor-market adjustment in a major economy. The score reflects possible consequence if implemented, not evidence that it has been implemented or achieved outcomes.
limitations: The evidence is the State Council Office’s own policy text; it establishes what the government announced, not whether all provisions are binding or implemented.
The opinion describes 18 measures across six areas but gives no quantified job-creation or displacement target, total budget, or uniform implementation deadline in the reviewed text.
It mentions using the National AI Industry Investment Fund as an existing instrument but announces no new allocation amount or project-level disbursement.
No employment, wage, productivity, retraining, or distributional outcome is measured; the opinion is not evidence of realized net job growth or reduced displacement.
organizations: General Office of the State Council of the People’s Republic of China
Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security
brief.summary: China’s General Office of the State Council published an opinion on 23 October 2026 (document date 16 October) setting out 18 measures in six areas for an employment-focused response to AI development. It calls for AI-related job creation and training while also addressing adoption-related job risk, worker transitions, employment services, labor and social-security protections, income distribution, and monitoring. The text directs risk assessment for potentially high-impact AI applications in market-access areas and calls for cautious pacing in labor-intensive sectors. It establishes announced policy direction, not implementation, funding totals, or measured employment effects.

technical.claimed_result: The opinion states policy goals and tasks for balancing AI-enabled development with high-quality employment, including expanding new AI-related occupations, supporting SMEs, encouraging human-machine collaboration, reducing transition harms, and building employment-risk monitoring. These are government-stated objectives, not demonstrated labor-market effects.
technical.compute_or_cost: No total budget or new allocation amount is specified in the reviewed text. It mentions use of the National AI Industry Investment Fund and other existing public investment instruments on a market-oriented basis.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official State Council portal publishes Guobanfa [2026] No. 29 and its text identifies six policy areas with 18 tasks. The page metadata distinguishes a 16 October document date from a 23 October publication date.
technical.implementation_status: Announced central policy opinion addressed to provincial governments, ministries and directly affiliated institutions; subordinate rules, deadlines, budget execution, local implementation and outcomes are not established here.
technical.mechanism: The opinion combines AI-sector and SME job creation, human-machine collaboration, cautious rollout in labor-intensive sectors, risk assessments for some market-access AI proposals, worker notice and transition support, skills training, AI-enabled employment services, labor/social-security protections, and employment monitoring/research.
technical.novelty: The opinion makes employment impact, job-transition support and employment-risk review explicit parts of China’s national AI-policy direction; it does not establish a new technical method or measured labor-market result.
technical.regime: National policy direction from China’s State Council General Office to provincial governments and central ministries; particular assessments and supports depend on future implementation.
technical.reproducibility: The policy text is available through the official government portal’s indexed Chinese content. This research review did not observe subordinate implementation instruments or implementation outcomes.
technical.strongest_baseline: The opinion builds on China’s existing AI+ action and high-quality employment policy context; it adds an explicit package of 18 AI-and-employment tasks. This record does not assess how it changes pre-existing legal requirements or local plans.

brief.title: China sets out national AI employment policy with worker-transition and job-risk measures
brief.why_it_matters: The opinion puts employment effects directly into national AI-adoption policy, tying AI expansion to worker transition support, skills, labor protections and risk assessment. These directions could shape deployment incentives and adjustment costs if implemented, but the document supplies no quantified employment target, new budget allocation, uniform deadline or evidence of labor-market outcomes.
